gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured charge current or measured charge time for any 48V lithium golf cart charger. The only named first-hand measurement found is Golfer Hive's (byline Mark Crossfield) on an EPOWREY 58.4V 18A charger: 17.8–18.2 A in bulk on an inline multimeter, 58.4 V peak before shutoff, and 5.5–6 h for a full 0–100% charge of a 105Ah pack on a Club Car DS.
standout_why: I compared against iwantgolf.com (cited), which says its products 'have not been independently bench-tested here' and gives only maker claims and its own arithmetic. Canyon Lake Mobile (rank 1) gives charge times as 'typical' estimates with no test method. golfcartgearlab.com (rank 6) says 'We did not run any batteries ourselves.' I couldn't extract text from the Trojan OnePack PDF (cited), but it's a compatibility guide. So no rival has a measured figure. Still, the one measurement I found is for a charger ChatGPT didn't show (EPOWREY, not LiTime, Vatrer or Lester). It comes from an affiliate page with thin documentation (no meter models, no ambient conditions, no logs). Its 5.5–6 h result only confirms the 6–7 h estimate ChatGPT already gave for an 18A charger.
decides: It doesn't change the pick. The measured 17.8–18.2 A shows that a budget 58.4V 18A charger can deliver its rated current. A full 105Ah charge in 5.5–6 h is consistent with ChatGPT's estimates, so it mildly supports the 'value 18A' tier. No named reviewer or lab has measured the actual candidates (Lester Summit II, LiTime 18A or 30A, Vatrer 20A), so the page can't rank them on measured performance. It should rank them on battery-maker profile approval and rated current.

findings.source_title: EPOWREY 48v LiFePO4 Charger Review: Worth the Upgrade? (Golfer Hive)
findings.note: Byline Mark Crossfield; page 'UPDATED: May 18, 2026'. Inline multimeter, model not given. 30-day test on a Club Car DS with a 105Ah lithium pack, about 5 charges a week. Affiliate page, and the byline (a UK golf coach and YouTuber) is unverified.

findings.source_title: EPOWREY 48v LiFePO4 Charger Review: Worth the Upgrade? (Golfer Hive)
findings.note: Digital multimeter, model not given. 58.4 V = 16 cells × 3.65 V, the standard LiFePO4 full-charge voltage.

findings.label: Measured full charge time, 0–100%
findings.source_title: EPOWREY 48v LiFePO4 Charger Review: Worth the Upgrade? (Golfer Hive)
findings.note: Ideal time is 105 Ah ÷ 18 A = 5.8 h, so the result fits a charger holding its rated current with a short constant-voltage taper. ChatGPT estimated 6–7 h for 18A on 100Ah.

findings.source_title: EPOWREY 48v LiFePO4 Charger Review: Worth the Upgrade? (Golfer Hive)
findings.note: Infrared thermal camera, 'on a hot day'. Ambient temperature and charge duration not given.

findings.note: Steve Hanley, July 3, 2026. Owner observation from a partial discharge. No starting charge level, no meter and no charger model, so it isn't a comparable measurement. It doesn't conflict with a 20A rating (105 Ah ÷ 20 A ≈ 5.3 h from empty).

unsourced: A measurement by a named reviewer or lab of the Lester Summit II 650W or 1050W (output current on a lithium profile, efficiency, charge time). I searched for reviews and forum measurements. Lester's 'at least 90% efficient' is a maker claim from dealer material, and I didn't open it.

A named bench test of the LiTime 48V 18A or 30A charger. Searches turned up only maker listings and owner comments. The LiTime product pages returned HTTP 429, and so did storecheck.py, so I couldn't read prices or on-page owner reports.
A named bench test of the Vatrer 58.4V 20A (listed by Vatrer as 22A) charger. I found only maker and retailer listings.
US DOE or California CEC lab-tested energy figures (unit energy consumption) for golf cart chargers. The DOE certification database query returned HTTP 403, and the CEC database wasn't reachable.
The Trojan OnePack charger compatibility PDF (cited by ChatGPT). WebFetch returned only the raw PDF, and I couldn't extract the text.
